descriptors.definition: The tax base of an asset or liability is the specific amount attributed to it for income tax purposes. It represents the deductible amount against taxable economic benefits that will flow to the entity upon recovering the carrying amount.
inclusion: Amount deductible against future taxable economic benefits
Cost less cumulative tax depreciation
exclusion: Accounting revaluations ignored for tax purposes
nearby_distinctions: Carrying amount reflects financial reporting value, whereas tax base is strictly determined by taxation laws.

descriptors.definition: Temporary differences are calculated as the difference between the carrying amount of an asset or liability in the balance sheet and its corresponding tax base. These differences ultimately reverse over time, resulting in a cumulative impact of zero.
inclusion: Differences between balance sheet carrying amount and tax base
Timing differences
nearby_distinctions: Temporary differences encompass timing differences but are broader because they also capture balance sheet carrying value adjustments like revaluations.

descriptors.definition: Temporary differences are categorized into taxable temporary differences, which increase future tax liabilities, and deductible temporary differences, which reduce them. This classification dictates whether a deferred tax liability or asset should be recognized.
inclusion: Taxable temporary differences arising when asset carrying amount exceeds tax base
Deductible temporary differences arising when liability carrying amount exceeds tax base
nearby_distinctions: Taxable temporary differences result in future taxable amounts, whereas deductible temporary differences generate future tax deductions.

descriptors.definition: Specific exceptions apply to the general recognition rules for deferred taxes, such as the initial recognition of goodwill in a business combination. In jurisdictions where goodwill is not tax-deductible, its tax base is nil and no deferred tax liability is recognized to avoid circular computations.
inclusion: Goodwill arising from business combinations where tax base is nil and not deductible
exclusion: Standard asset and liability temporary differences subject to routine deferred tax accounting
nearby_distinctions: Goodwill exceptions prevent the circular inflation of carrying values that would occur if deferred tax liabilities were recognized on residual goodwill.

descriptors.concept_name: Step 6: Assess (also reassess) deductible temporary differences, tax losses and tax credits
descriptors.definition: Deductible temporary differences and unused tax losses only provide economic benefits if the entity expects future taxable profits against which they can be utilized. Entities must assess and reassess the probability of sufficient future taxable profits to recognize deferred tax assets.
inclusion: Unused trading losses available for carry forward within legal limits
Assessment of future taxable profits
exclusion: Tax losses exceeding statutory carry-forward time limits
nearby_distinctions: Unlike taxable temporary differences that automatically create liabilities, deductible temporary differences and tax losses require positive profit evidence for asset recognition.

descriptors.definition: Deferred tax assets and liabilities must be measured using the tax rates and laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the end of the reporting period. These rates must reflect the expected manner of recovery or settlement of the asset or liability's carrying amount.
inclusion: Tax rates expected to apply during realization or settlement
Rates reflecting expected manner of asset recovery or liability settlement
exclusion: Tax rates enacted after the reporting period end
nearby_distinctions: Tax rates applied depend on whether an asset is recovered through use or sale if different statutory rates apply to each mode.

descriptors.concept_name: Step 8: Calculate and recognise deferred tax
descriptors.definition: Deferred tax balances are computed by multiplying taxable or deductible temporary differences by the applicable enacted tax rates. Recognized deferred tax assets must be reviewed at each reporting date and reduced if sufficient future taxable profits are no longer probable.
inclusion: Multiplication of temporary differences by applicable tax rates
Periodic review and adjustment of deferred tax asset carrying amounts
exclusion: Discounting of deferred tax assets and liabilities to present value
nearby_distinctions: Calculation yields gross temporary impacts that are strictly prohibited from being discounted under standard rules.

descriptors.definition: The accounting treatment for deferred tax effects must align with the underlying transaction or event, being recognized in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, or directly in equity. Subsequent changes in deferred tax balances driven by tax rate changes are also routed through profit or loss unless tied to prior non-P&L items.
inclusion: Tax effects recognized in profit or loss, OCI, or equity
Pro rata allocation for complex items recognized outside profit or loss
exclusion: Disconnecting tax accounting from the classification of the underlying economic event
nearby_distinctions: Items originating in equity or OCI mandate that their corresponding deferred tax adjustments bypass the statement of profit and loss.

descriptors.concept_name: Step 10: Offsetting deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities
descriptors.definition: Entities can offset deferred tax assets against deferred tax liabilities only if they possess a legally enforceable right to set off current tax assets against current tax liabilities. Furthermore, both deferred balances must relate to income taxes levied by the same taxation authority on the same taxable entity or qualifying distinct entities.
inclusion: Net presentation when legally enforceable set-off rights exist
Taxes levied by the same authority on the same or intentionally simultaneous settling entities
exclusion: Offsetting across different unrelated taxation authorities without legal rights
nearby_distinctions: Offsetting is restricted solely to instances with legal enforceability and matching tax jurisdictions, avoiding arbitrary aggregation.

descriptors.definition: Practical application of income tax standards involves recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities arising from fair value adjustments in business combinations. These recognized tax balances directly affect the determination of goodwill or bargain purchase gains on the acquisition date.
inclusion: Deferred tax impacts from asset and liability fair value uplifts in acquisitions
Adjustments to goodwill calculations
exclusion: Deferred tax liabilities on initial goodwill recognition exceptions
nearby_distinctions: Acquisition-date fair value adjustments create temporary differences that directly alter consolidated goodwill, distinguishing them from routine standalone asset shifts.

descriptors.concept_name: Deferred tax arising from a business combination
descriptors.definition: Temporary differences arising from fair value adjustments of identifiable assets and liabilities in a business combination require the recognition of resulting deferred tax assets or liabilities. These tax balances impact the quantum of goodwill or bargain purchase gain recognized at acquisition.
inclusion: Deferred tax on fair value adjustments of property, plant, equipment, and inventory
Impact on goodwill or bargain purchase
exclusion: Deferred tax liabilities on initial recognition of un-deductible goodwill
nearby_distinctions: Unlike routine internal asset revaluations, business combination fair valuation adjustments instantly integrate tax effects into acquisition accounting and goodwill.

descriptors.concept_name: Current and deferred tax arising from share-based payment transactions
descriptors.definition: Share-based payment remuneration expenses recognized under accounting standards often generate tax deductions in later periods or based on future share prices. The difference between the future tax deduction tax base and the nil carrying amount creates a deductible temporary difference and associated deferred tax asset.
inclusion: Tax deductions linked to employee share options
Deferred tax assets derived from estimated future share-price-based deductions
exclusion: Deductions exceeding cumulative remuneration expense which must be routed to equity
nearby_distinctions: Excess tax deductions over cumulative accounting remuneration expenses are segregated and recognized directly in equity rather than profit or loss.
